title: Il Condizionale Presente
subtitle: Would — for politeness, wishes, and advice.
objectives: Conjugate regular verbs in the condizionale presente
Use the conditional of dovere for advice

content.intro: The conditional is what makes Italian sound polite: vorrei instead of voglio, potrebbe instead of può — the single grammatical feature that softens a request into a courtesy.
content.explanation: The conditional shares the same irregular stems as the future (sar-, avr-, andr-, and so on) but takes its own distinct set of endings. It's used constantly in everyday speech for politeness, wishes, and giving advice.

rules.heading: a) Endings
rules.body: -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero, added to the same stem as the future (parler-, avr-, sar-...).

rules.heading: b) Politeness
rules.body: Vorrei (I would like) is the standard polite way to order or request, replacing the blunter voglio: Vorrei un caffè, per favore. Potrebbe aiutarmi? (Could you help me? — formal)

rules.heading: c) Advice with dovrei/dovresti
rules.body: Dovresti riposare di più. (You should rest more.) Softer and more natural than the blunt obligation of devi.

examples.it: Vorrei un tavolo per due, per favore.
examples.en: I would like a table for two, please.
I would love to visit Sicily.
It would be fantastic to travel together.

commonMistakes.wrong: Voglio un caffè. (as a polite order in a café)
commonMistakes.why: Voglio is grammatically fine but blunt — vorrei is the standard polite register for ordering or requesting.

commonMistakes.wrong: Dovrei che tu studi di più.
commonMistakes.why: Dovere + infinitive needs no conjunction che — it pairs directly with the infinitive, just like in the present tense.

commonMistakes.wrong: Io vorrei andare al mare. spelled voglierei
commonMistakes.right: vorrei (irregular stem vorr-, not a regular volere stem)
commonMistakes.why: Volere has an irregular conditional stem, vorr-, shared with the future — not a regular form built from the infinitive.

items.prompt: ___ (Volere - io) un bicchiere d'acqua, per favore.
items.explanation: Vorrei is the polite conditional of volere.
Conditional of potere, tu form: potresti.
Conditional of dovere, voi form: dovreste.

items.prompt: Ordering coffee politely at a café bar:
items.explanation: Vorrei is the standard polite conditional for ordering.

summary: The conditional shares the future's irregular stems, with its own endings: -ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero.
Vorrei/potrebbe soften requests into polite register — used constantly in daily life.
Dovrei/dovresti give gentle advice, softer than the direct obligation of devo/devi.
